comparison: Both evaluate the mathematical proof (C11, C17, C20, C21, C24, C30, C31, C32, C110-C113, C132) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes it as 'rigorous' and 'mathematically sound,' while peer reviewers call it 'mathematically well-defined' and 'internally consistent.' Both accept the proof's validity, though peer reviewers note it rests on key assumptions.

OpenEval finds the parsimony argument (C12, C34, C35, C114-C117) SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN. OpenEval accepts the teleological explanation (C117) as well-supported by efficiency principles. Peer reviewers explicitly challenge claims of definitive proof (C168, C117), stating the work 'does not provide proof of what grid cells are doing' due to functional assumptions.

Both evaluate the experimental prediction about field spacing (C36, C38, C39) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the prediction is 'close to' experimental data with reasonable explanations for discrepancy. Peer reviewers do not challenge this comparison and commend the authors for addressing experimental observations.

Both find the orientation prediction (C40-C44) SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the close match between predicted 10.9° and experimental median 9.8°. Peer reviewers acknowledge the model 'extends to explain several findings' including this prediction without specific challenge.

Both evaluate 1-D phenomena explanations (C45-C53) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights 'strong convergent evidence' from multiple experimental paradigms. Peer reviewers note the authors 'extend the model to explain several findings' and describe results as 'consistent with or predicted by their theory.'

Both find non-spatial domain extensions (C54-C57, C99-C103) SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the model's 'broader applicability' with well-cited evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge the authors consider 'a wide range of experimental results' including non-spatial coding as part of valuable explanatory scope.

Both evaluate grid map malleability explanations (C58-C66) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 'convergent evidence from multiple experimental paradigms strongly supports the model's explanatory power.' Peer reviewers find the explanation of malleability compelling as part of the model's consistency with experimental results.

Both rate grid map warping mechanism (C67-C76) as UNCERTAIN or acknowledge speculation. OpenEval explicitly notes the mechanism is 'speculative' and 'lacks direct experimental validation.' Peer reviewers accept the explanation as part of broader model consistency but note it rests on foundational assumptions.

Both find population-level properties (C77-C84) SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes 'strong' logical chain from model to predictions to data. Peer reviewers note the manuscript is 'internally consistent' with 'comparisons to experimental observations' for these population predictions.

Both evaluate modular organization explanation (C85-C89, C136-C139) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds the √2 scaling match with experimental data 'compelling.' Peer reviewers acknowledge the model 'extends to explain several findings' including modular organization as part of explanatory scope.

OpenEval finds sequence coding evidence (C13-C16, C96-C109) SUPPORTED with 'extensive' and 'convergent evidence.' Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, with one explicitly challenging that Gardner et al. supports sequences 'except in the most trivial sense' and noting this foundational assumption should be 'treated carefully.'

Both find path integration connections (C122-C131) SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes 'strong' integration of theory and experiment with 'convergent support.' Peer reviewers note the model demonstrates 'path integration is an important driving force' with appropriate comparisons to experimental observations.

Both evaluate the conformal isometry property (C132-C135) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes 'strong corroboration' from independent theoretical work (Xu et al., 2024; Schøyen et al., 2024). Peer reviewers accept this geometric property without challenge and commend reference updates.

OpenEval rates multiscale trajectory hypothesis (C136-C143) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's 'speculative' and 'requires substantial future work.' Peer reviewers rate the modular organization explanation (overlapping C136-C139) as SUPPORTED, accepting it as part of the model's explanatory framework without emphasizing the speculative nature.

Both find 3-D extension (C157-C166) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes 'strong' convergence of predictions and data from rats and bats. Peer reviewers acknowledge the authors consider 'a wide range of experimental results' and explicitly state not to 'hold up the authors to an impossible standard.'

OpenEval finds the claim of identifying underlying process (C167-C168) SUPPORTED as 'justified by the mathematical proof.' Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating the work 'does not provide proof' of grid cell function due to assumptions about biological function.

Both evaluate scope limitations (C169-C172) as SUPPORTED/acknowledged. OpenEval notes the limitations are 'appropriate and honest' and 'don't undermine the main theoretical contribution.' Peer reviewers accept the limitation that mechanism remains obscure as appropriate for normative theory.

Both find the background and motivation (C1-C10, C5-C6, C8-C9) SUPPORTED. OpenEval states the framing 'effectively motivates the work.' Peer reviewers acknowledge the recognized gap that 'a specific and intuitive answer to why grid cells have evolved has remained elusive.'

Both evaluate critique of prior approaches (C91-C95) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds the assessment 'fair and well-cited' and 'effectively positions the current work's contribution.' Peer reviewers accept this as motivation, though emphasize the current work also rests on assumptions.

Both find the critique of normative neural network models (C118-C121) SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the critique about 'mechanistic opacity' and 'hyperparameter dependence' is 'fair and accurate.' Peer reviewers accept this assessment as context for the study.

OpenEval evaluates model assumptions and limitations (C144-C153) as SUPPORTED, noting 'honest acknowledgment of assumptions and their implications strengthens the overall work.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about assumption relaxation and path integration errors.

OpenEval finds extensions to cognitive functions and Alzheimer's (C154-C156) SUPPORTED, noting the model 'provides a coherent framework for understanding these clinical observations.' No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these clinical relevance claims.

OpenEval evaluates mathematical foundations (C18, C19, C33) as SUPPORTED, noting 'these mathematical foundations are solid' with proper citations to proven results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mathematical facts.
